benefits.title: King’s gets greater value from its physical estate in the student experience
benefits.statement: King’s campuses become richer settings for student life beyond scheduled study, with more visible, low-friction invitations to connect, participate and access broader opportunities. The estate contributes more actively to belonging, participation, graduate futures and students’ sense of the value they gain from university life.
benefits.successLooksLike: Student footfall grows in campus spaces and activities beyond scheduled study, alongside increasing attendance at campus-based opportunities and events.

benefits.title: Students who are less campus-present gain a legitimate space for participation beyond their courses
benefits.statement: King’s develops a growing blended, digital and distance extracurricular offer through which students who cannot regularly engage with campus can participate meaningfully in communities, activities and opportunities beyond their courses. These experiences become a legitimate and authentic part of student life rather than a lesser substitute for physical participation.
benefits.beneficiary: Students who are less or never campus-present
benefits.successLooksLike: The blended, digital and distance offer expands over time, with increasing attendances and repeat participation from students who are less or never campus-present.
